name: Azure Data Explorer
tagline: Microsoft's Kusto engine: fast KQL analytics over logs, telemetry and time series at petabyte scale.
description: Azure Data Explorer is the managed form of Kusto, the append-optimised columnar engine that also underpins Azure Monitor Log Analytics, Microsoft Sentinel and Fabric Real-Time Intelligence (Eventhouse). It ingests streaming and batch data from Event Hubs, IoT Hub, Kafka and storage, indexes every column including free text and dynamic JSON, and answers Kusto Query Language queries with built-in time-series functions such as make-series, anomaly detection and forecasting. Microsoft's newer investment is Fabric Eventhouse, which runs the same engine, but standalone ADX clusters remain fully supported; only the Synapse-integrated variant was retired, in October 2025.

pricing.notes: Billed per cluster compute and storage; a free personal cluster is available for trials.

scale.notes: Compute nodes cache hot extents on SSD over blob storage; follower databases expose data to clusters in other regions.

strengths: KQL is expressive for log and telemetry exploration, with built-in series, anomaly and forecasting functions
Indexes every column, including free text and dynamic JSON, by default
Same engine and query language as Azure Monitor, Sentinel and Fabric Eventhouse
Ingests directly from Event Hubs, IoT Hub and Kafka with low latency
Materialized views and update policies for ingestion-time transforms
weaknesses: Cluster-based pricing can be costly at low utilisation
Product direction is shifting toward Fabric, which complicates long-term planning
Not designed for row-level updates or transactional workloads
useCases: Interactive dashboards over billions of events
notIdealFor: Small datasets that fit a single Postgres
